title: kbmon --metrics: a snapshot as metric points with id-only, redacted attributes
goal: python3 _tools/kbmon.py --metrics prints one JSON object whose points each carry a name starting kbmon., a unit, a kind (gauge or sum), a value and attributes whose values are numbers, flags or ids that passed redact.redact, with no holder attribute; the kb facts point for root public and tag DOC equals rag.py audit's count

clauses.clause: python3 _tools/kbmon.py --metrics prints one JSON object whose points each carry a name starting kbmon., a unit, a kind (gauge or sum), a value and attributes whose values are numbers, flags or ids that passed redact.redact, with no holder attribute
the kb facts point for root public and tag DOC equals rag.py audit's count

gates.question: Does an exported metric carry a claim's holder?
options: no: claims are counted by state, the key only when it is a backlog item id
yes, when the holder is an id
gates.recommendation: no: claims are counted by state, the key only when it is a backlog item id
gates.answer: no: claims are counted by state, the key only when it is a backlog item id

gates.question: Which names do kbmon's metrics take?
options: kbmon.<panel>.<measure>, e.g. kbmon.kb.facts with root and tag
gates.recommendation: kbmon.<panel>.<measure>, e.g. kbmon.kb.facts with root and tag
gates.answer: kbmon.<panel>.<measure>, e.g. kbmon.kb.facts with root and tag

gates.question: How does --metrics treat an attribute value that is no number, flag or redaction-stable identifier?
options: the whole point is left out
gates.recommendation: the whole point is left out
gates.answer: the whole point is left out

gates.question: Which flag selects the metrics output and which points does it carry beyond the panels' data?
options: --metrics beside --json and --once; every panel's up and seconds, kb, coord and sessions measures, the alert count
--metrics with the kb and coord measures only
gates.recommendation: --metrics beside --json and --once; every panel's up and seconds, kb, coord and sessions measures, the alert count
gates.answer: --metrics beside --json and --once; every panel's up and seconds, kb, coord and sessions measures, the alert count

notes: Plan 2026-10-18: the stdlib side owns the allowlist and the redaction, so the SDK adapter only forwards points it is given and the leak guard runs without the SDK. The planted snapshot holds one fake secret of each kbcommon.SECRETS shape and a key=value assignment, built at run time.
